core_obligations: Reduce to affine Y using base change of the relative dualizing complex, and prove (1) by identifying Rf_*(E otimes^L omega) with the dual of Rf_*E^vee and applying the criterion for relative perfectness (proof lines 3045-3070).
Prove (2) by rewriting Hom_Y(M, Rf_*omega) as Hom_Y(M otimes^L Rf_*O_X, O_Y) and testing against M = O_Y[-i] for i > 0 using the tor amplitude bound (proof lines 3072-3092).

Prove (3) by the seven term chain evaluating Hom_X(E, RSheafHom(omega, omega)) first, then producing alpha from E = O_X and concluding with the generation statement that the cone of alpha vanishes (proof lines 3094-3156).
proof_roadmap: Reduction to affine Y and the proof of (1) (proof lines 3045-3070).
The proof of (2) via the tor amplitude of Rf_*O_X (proof lines 3072-3092).
The chain of equalities for (3) (proof lines 3094-3122).
The map alpha and the generation argument (proof lines 3124-3156).
difficulty_reason: For a quasi-compact and quasi-separated Y and a proper flat finite presentation f : X -> Y with relative dualizing complex omega, the lemma asserts three properties: omega is Y-perfect, Rf_*omega has no cohomology in positive degrees, and O_X -> RSheafHom(omega, omega) is an isomorphism (statement lines 3027-3043). Because the formation of omega commutes with base change by Remark labelled remark-relative-dualizing-complex, the proof may assume Y affine (proof lines 3045-3049). For (1) it computes, for a perfect E, that Rf_*(E otimes^L omega) equals (Rf_*E^vee)^vee by three steps, using Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-dual-perfect-complex, Lemma labelled lemma-iso-on-RSheafHom with Remark labelled remark-iso-on-RSheafHom and Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-flat-proper-perfect-direct-image-general, and the definition of the dual, concluding Y-perfectness by More on Morphisms, Lemma labelled more-morphisms-lemma-characterize-relatively-perfect (proof lines 3051-3070). For (2) it rewrites Hom_Y(M, Rf_*omega) as Hom_Y(M otimes^L Rf_*O_X, O_Y) using adjunction, the construction of a, and Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-cohomology-base-change; since Rf_*O_X is perfect of tor amplitude in [0, N] by Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-flat-proper-perfect-direct-image-general and Y is affine, it is represented by a complex of finite projective modules in degrees [0, N] by More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-perfect, so taking M = O_Y[-i] with i > 0 gives zero and hence the vanishing (proof lines 3072-3092). For (3) the proof writes a seven term chain of equalities for Hom_X(E, RSheafHom(omega, omega)) ending at Hom_X(E, O_X), using Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-internal-hom, the construction of omega, dualisation for perfect complexes by Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-dual-perfect-complex, the identity from the first paragraph, double duality, and Leray (proof lines 3094-3122). To conclude, the proof notes that RSheafHom(omega, omega) lies in D_QCoh by Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-quasi-coherence-internal-hom, takes E = O_X to get the map alpha corresponding to the identity, and uses that the cone of alpha has vanishing Hom from every perfect object together with the generation statement of Derived Categories of Schemes, Theorem labelled perfect-theorem-bondal-van-den-Bergh to conclude that alpha is an isomorphism via the Yoneda lemma (proof lines 3124-3156). Computing the pushforward in terms of the dual of Rf_*E, and converting a functorial family of isomorphisms into an isomorphism by generation, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
